newsitem.title: UK: Russia may seek lower limit on debt deal - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Russia may seek lower limit on debt deal - dealers.

text.p: Russia is meeting with the London Club of commercial bank creditors on Wednesday and may propose to lower the threshold necessary to close its debt restructuring agreement, dealers in London said.
"Russia is going to the table today proposing to reduce the threshold to 75 percent from 90 percent," said a head Brady bond trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
He said the bank steering committee would be reluctant to lower the limit to 75 percent but might agree to 80 to 85 percent critical mass.
Under current terms, Russia needs to fully reconcile 90 percent of the $24 billion principal of its total $35 billion debt owed to the London Club.
Bankers said officials from the London Club steering committee head Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Vneshekonombank and the ministry of finance were meeting on Wednesday to discuss the proposals.
In addition, traders said they were expecting Russia to announce the latest figure of debt that has been fully reconciled with the banks.
"We expect to hear later today from the meeting. We are waiting to hear what level of the debt has been reconciled," the trader added.
Last week, Russia said 60 percent of its outstanding debt had been fully reconciled with the banks. It also promised to start publishing fully reconciled volumes every week beginning in August.
